title: AAR Contents, Resources, Consumer Rules, and Publication

scout.purpose: Master aar contents, resources, consumer rules, and publication through a production or platform contract supported by causal evidence.
scout.realWorldUse: Specialist Android work must remain compatible, secure, measurable, accessible, distributable, and operable outside a demonstration.
scout.outcome: You can design, inspect, test, release, and defend aar contents, resources, consumer rules, and publication.

blocks.text: An AAR can package classes, manifest, resources, assets, native libraries, lint checks, public resource metadata, and consumer R8 rules. The consuming app merges and optimises these inputs, so conflicts and hidden assumptions surface outside the library build. Prefix resources, declare only intended public resources, minimise manifest components and permissions, and use consumer rules narrowly for reflection, JNI, serialization, or callbacks that R8 cannot see. Never package keep-all rules as a support shortcut.

blocks.text: Publication includes artifact, POM, Gradle module metadata, sources, documentation, checksums, signatures or attestations, license and provenance. Variant attributes and dependencies must describe compile and runtime needs accurately; publishing internal debug or flavor dimensions can burden consumers. Use api only when dependency types are part of public ABI and implementation otherwise. Pin or constrain responsibly without forcing unrelated dependency versions. Test the repository artifact, not the local project substitution that bypasses metadata.

blocks.caption: A focused fragment whose complete contract includes exact versions, ownership, adverse paths, compatibility, and release evidence.

blocks.text: Create a temporary Maven repository and matrix consumer projects for min SDK, namespace, resource collision, manifest merge, Kotlin and Java, R8 full mode, missing optional dependency, offline resolution, and supported AGP or Gradle. Inspect the AAR and metadata before release. Verify deterministic coordinates, immutable versions, reproducible artifact identity, SBOM and dependency licenses, and rollback through a corrected new version rather than replacing published bytes.

Expert engineering makes assumptions, authority, compatibility, security, privacy, accessibility, performance, distribution, and recovery reviewable. Begin with a concrete user or platform outcome, identify trust and lifecycle boundaries, and retain exact source, dependency, toolchain, configuration, model or platform version, and artifact identity. Test realistic success plus denial, offline, process death, cancellation, corruption, version skew, resource pressure, and dependency failure. Measure representative distributions rather than best runs. Document unsupported cases, residual risk, owners, release gates, incident response, deprecation, and rollback or roll-forward. A specialised solution is production-ready only when another team can integrate, verify, operate, upgrade, disable, and remove it safely.

blocks.title: Expert trap
blocks.text: Watch carefully for this common failure mode in production: Testing only with an included project can pass even when the published POM or Gradle metadata omits a runtime dependency.

inspect.expectedOutput: A reproducible expert artifact or investigation with explicit contracts, limitations, evidence, and operational ownership.

trap_check.mistake: Testing only with an included project can pass even when the published POM or Gradle metadata omits a runtime dependency.
trap_check.why: It hides an ownership, compatibility, trust, lifecycle, or evidence gap that becomes costly outside the demonstration.
trap_check.fix: Make the disputed boundary explicit and add a representative negative or compatibility test plus operational response.

trap_check.mistake: Treating one successful device, client, model, platform build, or release as proof of the supported contract.
trap_check.why: Advanced Android ecosystems contain version, hardware, consumer, policy, and runtime variation.
trap_check.fix: Define the support matrix and verify exact artifacts across representative and adverse conditions.

challenge_intro.task: Publish a namespaced minified AAR to a temporary repository and prove metadata, resources, manifest, dependencies, consumer rules, provenance, and matrix consumption.
challenge_intro.successLooksLike: The work includes a minimal coherent implementation, exact evidence, support and threat boundaries, adverse testing, release operation, and recovery.

recall.prompt: Who applies a library consumer R8 rule?
recall.answer: The consuming application shrinker applies rules packaged in the library while optimizing the final app.

recall.prompt: What must accompany an expert Android artifact?
recall.answer: Exact source and build identity, supported versions, contracts, tests, measurements, security and privacy review, release evidence, owner, and recovery plan.
They prevent consumers and operators from treating an untested or impossible condition as a silent guarantee.
